seo.title: DoorDash: causal targeting of promotions - cost per incremental order cut by nearly half (2025)
seo.meta_description: DoorDash targets its promotions with causal machine learning: by estimating the incremental effect per customer, the personalized approach cuts cost per incremental order by nearly half at equal lift.
seo.resume_citable: DoorDash targets its promotions with causal machine learning by estimating each customer's uplift; the personalized approach cuts cost per incremental order by nearly half at equal sales performance.

faq.q: How does DoorDash decide who to send a promotion to?
faq.a: A causal machine learning model estimates, for each customer, the incremental effect of the promo on their order probability, then the allocation is optimized under a budget constraint.

faq.q: What does causal targeting of promotions gain?
faq.a: At equal sales performance, the personalized approach cuts cost per incremental order by nearly half compared with a uniform send.

objectif_business: Spend the promotional budget where it actually creates additional orders, instead of subsidizing orders that would have happened without a promo.
description: DoorDash uses causal machine learning to estimate the incremental effect of a promotion on each user's order probability, then chooses which promos to send under a budget constraint. The framework has two stages: first estimate the causal response per customer with methods like double machine learning and meta-learners, then optimize offer allocation. The problem it addresses is non-incremental promotions, where a discount rewards an order that would have happened anyway and burns margin. The work was presented at the causal ML workshop at KDD 2025.
points_cles: Causal targeting of promotions: incremental effect estimated per customer, then allocation under budget.
In-house causal framework (double machine learning, T-learner and S-learner meta-learners).
Cost per incremental order cut by nearly half at equal lift.
Evidence B, confirmed status, presented at the causal ML workshop at KDD 2025.

resultats.metrique: Cost per incremental order reduced, at equal lift, personalized versus uniform
Problem addressed by causal targeting, promo not targeted per individual

niveau_preuve.justification: Technical paper from the DoorDash teams presented at the causal ML workshop at KDD 2025, with a quantified result (cost per incremental order cut by nearly two), plus a concordant official engineering post. No consolidated financial figure, hence level B.

stack_technique.detail: Two-stage framework: per-customer uplift estimation (double machine learning, T-learner and S-learner meta-learners), presented at the causal ML workshop at KDD 2025.
Chooses which customers get which offer to maximize incremental orders within the fixed promo budget.
Internal channels through which the targeted promotions are delivered, then the real incremental is measured to retrain the model.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Per campaign, with uplift estimation before the send and incremental measurement after.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The estimated causal uplift per customer, that is the difference in order probability with and without the promo. Without a causal measurement, correlation is mistaken for effect and the budget scatters across non-incremental orders.

etapes.detail: The marketing team sets the objective and budget of the promotional campaign.
A causal model estimates the incremental effect of the promo on each customer's order probability.
The system chooses which customers to target to maximize incremental orders under the budget constraint.
The targeted offers are sent, then the real incremental is measured to retrain the model.

prerequis_data: order history with exposure to promos
results from experiments or natural variation to anchor the causal estimate
prerequis_orga: a data science team comfortable with causal inference
a promo budget steerable by segment
stack_possible: double machine learning and meta-learners for uplift
replication.premiere_etape: Estimate the causal uplift of an existing promo on a segment, then compare uplift-based targeting to a uniform send.

playbook.action: Audit the promo history: offer exposures, orders, a stable customer identifier.
playbook.livrable: An exposure-outcome dataset ready for modeling

playbook.action: Build the uplift estimation (double machine learning or meta-learners) on a past promo.
playbook.livrable: An uplift model validated offline (uplift by decile, Qini curves)

playbook.action: Add budget-constrained allocation optimization and define the test campaign.
playbook.livrable: A campaign plan: an uplift-targeted arm against a uniform arm, fixed budget

playbook.action: Run the controlled test, uplift-based targeting against a uniform send.
playbook.livrable: A read on cost per incremental order for both arms

playbook.action: Industrialize: retraining per campaign and systematic incremental measurement.
playbook.livrable: A reusable causal promo pipeline for every campaign

replication.equipe: 2 data scientists comfortable with causal inference + 1 growth PM + 1 CRM operator for the send.

statut_vivant.note: Causal framework described as applied to DoorDash's real marketing scenarios, documented by an official paper and engineering post.

transposable_ue.note: Causal targeting of promotions is transferable, but individual profiling to personalize an offer requires a GDPR legal basis and information about the automated decision logic. The causal analysis itself remains neutral under the AI Act.
